item.title: What You Can Achieve with Android-Driven Screen Hardware
item.description: Many companies search for affordable, flexible display options that work across different locations. Teams want systems that update quickly, stay reliable, and reduce long-term costs. These needs push businesses toward screen tools that support higher efficiency and simple control. Brands also look for ways to keep content fresh without buying heavy hardware.

item.title: Effective Tips To Prevent Eye Strain
item.description: Working on a laptop or scrolling through a phone can leave your eyes feeling tired and dry. Small changes in your habits can result in big improvements in how your eyes feel at the end of the day. Take control of your visual health with a few simple adjustments to your routine and environment.

item.title: Simple Structural Checks For Peace Of Mind At Home
item.description: Owning a home brings a lot of pride and a few worries about upkeep. Staying ahead of potential problems keeps your living space safe and saves money over time. You do not need to be a construction expert to spot trouble early. Most issues give off subtle hints before they turn into major repairs.

item.title: Temporary weekend closure of River Road planned for culvert replacement work
item.description: River Road will temporarily close to through traffic between Brownswood Road and Main Road beginning Friday, February 27 at 7 p.m., as crews replace an existing culvert near the intersection as part of the ongoing U.S. 17 and Main Road improvements.

item.title: New Poll: Overwhelming Majority of South Carolina Voters Support Regulated Hemp Products; Reject Statewide Ban
item.description: A new statewide survey shows South Carolinians overwhelmingly support keeping all hemp-derived products legally available in the state, when paired with reasonable, responsible regulation.

item.title: South Carolina Room at Main Library to Temporarily Close Ahead of Renovation
item.description: Charleston County Public Library’s (CCPL) South Carolina Room, located at the Main Library on 68 Calhoun Street, will temporarily close to the public beginning May 1, 2026 as the building prepares for renovation later this year.
